card.title: We Keep Switching Places
card.instruction: Return to a familiar relationship pattern, then reverse who performs each role whenever the scene reaches similar pressure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The projector's dead. Usually I talk you down, but today I need you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can use my laptop. Nobody's going to die.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep saying that while I imagine twelve directors sharing one screen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My laptop's dead too. We're finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody's going to die. I'll print twelve copies. You count them; twelve is less frightening when it's just paper.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 names the usual calming role now reversed; B2 takes it, and A5 reclaims it when B4 repeats the equipment-failure pressure.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 laptop solution causes A3 small-screen fear; B4 second failure causes A5 paper fallback and a calming task for B.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a real workaround before B4 loses confidence, and A5 responds practically rather than mocks B.

heightening.evidence: B4 panic shifts A5 into the reassuring role using the same phrase and an alternative for the same twelve directors.

specificity.evidence: A1 failed projector and A3 director count establish the presentation problem; A5 copies address that exact audience.
